query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.hypothesis: A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy processed via 40 hours of mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at optimized temperature (e.g., 1100-1200°C) will achieve a nanocrystalline grain size below 50 nm with a dual-phase solid solution structure consisting of two distinct BCC solid solutions, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar elemental powders of Nb, Mo, Ta, W, V, and Ti (NbMoTaWVTi)
generation.intervention: Mechanical alloying (ball milling) for 40 hours followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at optimized temperature and pressure
generation.conditions: Vacuum or inert atmosphere during processing; SPS temperature between 1100-1200°C; pressure ~50-100 MPa; holding time 5-10 minutes
generation.structural_mediator: Two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions formed during mechanical alloying, with grain refinement achieved through severe plastic deformation and rapid consolidation
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening from nanocrystalline structure (<50 nm) combined with solid solution strengthening from multiple principal elements; dual-phase BCC structure prevents brittle intermetallic formation while maintaining ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Compressive yield strength >2700 MPa, fracture strength >3100 MPa, total fracture strain >10%, with nanocrystalline grain size <50 nm and dual-phase BCC solid solution structure
generation.baseline: Conventional cast NbMoTaWVTi alloy with coarse grain structure and limited ductility due to brittle phase formation
generation.boundary: Grain coarsening above 1200°C during SPS; formation of brittle intermetallic phases (silicides, B2, Laves) if cooling rate is too slow or if oxygen contamination occurs; loss of nanocrystalline structure above 800°C during service
generation.uncertainty: Exact grain size distribution may vary with milling parameters; potential for TiO formation if oxygen contamination occurs during processing; thermal stability of nanocrystalline structure at elevated temperatures requires further validation
generation.falsification_experiment: Process NbMoTaWVTi alloy using identical mechanical alloying and SPS parameters but vary the SPS temperature above 1300°C and below 1000°C. Measure grain size via TEM and phase constitution via XRD. If grain size exceeds 50 nm or if brittle intermetallic phases form at any temperature, the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, perform tensile testing to verify if yield strength remains above 2700 MPa and ductility above 10% across the temperature range.

Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties
